newsitem.title: USA: Stock prices slip on profit-taking after blistering run.
newsitem.headline: Stock prices slip on profit-taking after blistering run.

text.p: Stocks were slightly lower in early trading Thursday as investors cooled their heels after the previous day's blistering run through the 8,000 level of the Dow Jones industrial average.
Shortly after 10:00 a.m. EDT, the blue-chip index was off 25.25 points at 8,013.33 in a modest retreat following Wednesday's 63-point jump.

The Nasdaq composite index was also subdued, as it slipped 13.24 points to 1,567.39 after Wednesday's 39-point gain went into the record books as the largest one-day rise and its 10th straight record high.
Analysts said the market drew a normal profit-taking reaction. But some believed that a steady stream of corporate earnings, which has propelled stocks higher, could provide fresh buying impetus.
Stocks have been tearing into record ground on a batch of hot earnings reports and good inflation news.
"The momentum is there and the earnings reports have been good," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"We should go higher even from a technical standpoint," he said. "As we approach options expiry tomorrow, that should fuel the markets' upward momentum."
The bond market was flat after the weekly jobless claims fell to 347,000, near economists' expectations of a drop to 345,000.
June housing starts data also came in close to expectations, rising to a 1.452 million unit annual rate.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond held at Wednesday's close of 6.48 percent.
